HomeEssentials Inc. - Q3 Earnings Call Transcript

Operator:
Good morning, everyone, and welcome to the HomeEssentials Inc. Q3 Earnings Conference Call. All participants will be in listen-only mode. After today's presentation, there will be an opportunity to ask questions. As a reminder, during the Q&A session, please limit yourself to one question and one follow-up. Please also note, today's event is being recorded.

I would now like to turn the conference over to Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations. Please go ahead.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
Thank you, Operator. Good morning, and thank you for joining us today to discuss HomeEssentials Inc.'s results for the third quarter. Joining me on today’s call are Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer; Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer; Lisa Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer; and David Kwon, Chief Stores Officer.

Before we begin, I would like to remind you that this call contains forward-looking statements, which are subject to risks and uncertainties. Please refer to our SEC filings for a complete discussion of these risks.

With that, I’ll turn the call over to Johnathan.

Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you, Sarah. Good morning, everyone. Thank you for joining us today. I’m pleased to report HomeEssentials Inc.'s performance for the third quarter. We continued to execute on our strategic priorities and delivered solid results despite the challenging macroeconomic environment.

Today I will cover six key aspects of our performance. First, our overall company performance highlights showed resilience in a choppy retail landscape. We achieved solid top-line growth, expanded margins via disciplined inventory management, and advanced our omnichannel strategy amid ongoing inflation, a weak housing market, and high interest rates impacting big-ticket durables.

The headline figures included consolidated net revenues of $2.48 billion, up 4.8% year-over-year, marking six consecutive quarters of growth. This exceeded our guidance midpoint and Wall Street expectations of $2.42 billion. Comparable store sales increased 3.2%, with traffic up 2.1% and average ticket rising 1.0% to $128. Essentials like paint, tools, and seasonal outdoor products performed strongly, countering softer demand for premium appliances and furniture, consistent with a 15% drop in existing home sales reported by the National Association of Realtors through September.

Gross profit reached $950 million, or 38.3% of sales, expanding 120 basis points from 37.1% last year. Key drivers were pricing discipline on private-label items, now 28% of assortments, and a 250-basis-point shrink reduction from RFID pilots in 450 stores. Freight costs eased to 4.2% of COGS from 5.1%, aided by nearshoring with Mexican suppliers for hardlines. Adjusted EBITDA was $285 million at an 11.5% margin, up 90 basis points, thanks to 15% comp flow-through and SG&A held at 27.2% of sales despite wage pressures.

Diluted EPS hit $1.12, up 18% and beating our $0.98 guide, supported by a $50 million share repurchase from our $500 million program. Free cash flow was outstanding at $320 million, funding $120 million in capex for remodels and digital while reducing net debt to 1.8x EBITDA.

By segment, our 1,850 U.S. brick-and-mortar stores, driving 78% of revenue, posted +3.5% comps, beating the ICD Retail Index by 180 basis points. E-commerce, 22% of sales, grew 12% to $545 million, with BOPIS up 28%. Services like installations and our HomePro loyalty program with 14 million members added $180 million, up 9%, with 22% attach rates.

Regionally, the Sun Belt shone with +5.8% comps from DIY traffic in Florida and Texas new home starts, similar to Tractor Supply trends. Midwest comps were +2.9% on millwork and flooring. Northeast managed +0.8% despite wet weather, West Coast +1.2% amid wildfires, and our 120 Canadian stores +4.1% in local currency against Canadian Tire.

Our three pillars drove this: supply chain resilience with 22% shorter lead times from Memphis DC expansion and vendor portals, dodging Red Sea issues; tech experiences like AI pricing on 15,000 SKUs for 3% comp lift and AR app boosting kitchen conversions 35%; store optimization with 180 remodels to 45,000 sq ft small formats lifting sales per sq ft to $1,250, up 8%, plus 12 openings and 9 closures for top-quartile productivity versus Home Depot and Lowe's.

We're gaining share as category traffic flattened per Placer.ai, but our dwell time rose 1.8% from tool rental hubs in 40% of stores. Our big-box project expertise yields 2-point NPS gain to 78 against Amazon and Walmart.

Q4 guidance: $2.65-2.72 billion revenue, +2.5-4.0% comps, 38.5% gross margin, $1.35-1.45 EPS, with holiday prep and $1.2 billion FY24 capex for 200 remodels and 30% digital mix by 2025.

Second, comparable store sales growth year-over-year was strong at +3.2%, accelerating from Q2's +3.2% wait no, strongest since pre-2022 peaks, with first-half at +3.3% toward full-year +4.0-5.0% midpoint. This generated significant comp revenue within our $2.48 billion total, including new stores and e-comm BOPIS.

Comps levers: traffic +2.1% from loyalty app check-ins up 12% and geofencing; conversion +1.0% to near 28% via AI 'Home Advisor' kiosks guiding 15% of shoppers on big-ticket like remodels; AUR +0.5% to $128, ATV +1.0% to around $300 on 22% service attach from HomePro installs.

Categories led by kitchen/bath +8.2% on private-label HearthStone gaining share vs IKEA; furniture/decor +6.1% from lifestyle zones up dwell 18%; softgoods +4.3% via DTC collabs like Brooklinen; outdoor +1.2% weather-hit but lapping easy comps.

Regions: Sunbelt (42% stores) +8.4% on migration/housing; Northeast +2.1% rate-pressured; Midwest +4.7%; West +3.9% offset by regs.

Initiatives: 180 Store 2.0 remodels with BOPIS bays to 18% store sales; 28M loyalty members +22% usage for 3.2 pps comps; inventory to 112 days; PROS pricing holding margins.

Against peers, outpacing Home Depot/Lowe's on affordable luxury; macro tailwinds millennial ownership, Fed cuts. Q4 comps +3.5-4.5%.

Third, traffic versus ticket breakdown revealed balanced comps of 3.2%, with 2.1% traffic gain—strongest in quarters—and 1.0% average ticket lift, ahead of industry -1.1% traffic and 0.8% ticket per Placer.ai.

By segment: home essentials flat traffic but +4% ticket on private ForgeHome; apparel +3% traffic +2% ticket back-to-school; seasonal +4% traffic +1.5% outdoor.

Trends: traffic accelerating, conversion +80bps to 28.5% express checkouts; regions Sunbelt +6.2% comps 4.8% traffic; Midwest +3.1%; Northeast +1.8%; West +5.9%.

Omnichannel: BOPIS 11% traffic, 65% add-ons; AI planograms +3.2% ticket; app personalization +7% basket; Uber tie-ins +8% visits. Capex $250M 60/40 traffic/ticket. Q3 comps +3.5-4.5%, traffic +2-2.5%.

We are confident in our ability to navigate the current environment and deliver long-term value for our shareholders.

Now, I'll turn the call over to Michael to provide more details on our financial results.

Michael Chen, Chief Financial Officer:
Thank you, Johnathan. Good morning. I'll provide a more detailed review of our financial performance for the third quarter.

Our total revenue for the quarter was $2.48 billion, a 4.8% increase compared to the same period last year. Gross margin was 38.3%, primarily driven by private-label pricing, shrink reduction, and lower freight. Operating expenses were $672 million, representing 27.2% of revenue. Net income was $210 million, or $1.12 per share. We generated $320 million in cash flow from operations. Inventory levels are currently $1.18 billion, down 12% year-over-year.

Fourth, on earnings guidance for next quarter and year, Q4 FY2024 revenue guides to $2.65-2.72 billion, 4-7% growth, comps +2.5-4.5% strong Sunbelt housing, BOPIS 28% e-comm. Gross 38.5-39.5%, +100bps from 15% freight cuts Maersk, AI forecasting 5.2x turns, 26% private-label. Op income $320-350M, 11.2-11.9% margin, SG&A flat despite wages, EPS $1.35-1.45 at 24.5% tax, 15M shares post buyback.

FY2025 revenue $11.7-12.1B, 3-6% growth, comps flat to +3%, H2 reaccel Fed cuts 4.2% unemployment. 150 remodels RFID <1% shrink, 20 micro-fulfillment 35% omni; Capex $450M 60% stores 25 net new Sunbelt 15k sq ft +20% productivity; EBITDA 12-13% RetailOS dynamic pricing +7% basket, 28% private-label ESG; 50% FCF returns $1.2B. Risks geo freight +10-15%, PCE >2.5%; upside housing 1.4M starts, 40% rewards adoption +2 comps.

Fifth, inventory levels year-over-year declined 12% to $1.18 billion from $1.34 billion, fourth straight quarter down, comp basis -14%, lowest pre-pandemic. Turns 5.2x from 4.1x, WOS 11.2 from 14.8, inv/sales 28% -400bps, markdowns 8.2% vs 11.5% +50bps margin.

Categories: home essentials -18% to $415M 85% full-price; apparel/softlines -22% to $295M AI forecast cut 30% slow-movers full-price 72%; furniture/hardlines -9% $236M 95% in-stock +7% comps; electronics/toys -7% $234M NPD aligned.

Regions: NE/Midwest -15% micro-fulfillment BOPIS 35%; South/West -10% 10.1 WOS RFID 98% accuracy.

Pillars: supply multi-source lead times -25% to 45 days forward contracts 70%; tech Trax scanning 99% compliance -40% OOS cull 12k SKUs; demand app heat maps pull-model excess <5%.

Q4 trough $1.1B +7% seq holiday 85% receipted 60% private +1500bps margin. Unlocked $75M capital repurchases dividend hikes.

Sixth, gross margin percentage year-over-year expanded 120 basis points to 38.3% from 37.1%, strongest in years, on track full-year 38.0-38.5%.

Drivers: mix +80bps private-label/owned 28% from 24%, HomeEssentials line >45% vs low-20s third-party; supply/procure +60bps 65% Mexico/Vietnam freight 4.2% from 5.1% DFW DC Sunbelt turns 5.8x +150bps NE offset; tech inv mgmt +40bps AI forecast 92% markdowns -25% RFID 85% stores shrink 1.1%.

Headwinds: promo -40bps EDLP match Walmart COGS +1.2% from +4.5% tariffs 10bps e-comm 14% +300bps gap narrowed; H2 +100bps private 30% micro-fulfillment.

This validates store-centric with Ulta shop-in-shops +200bps beauty.

We are maintaining a strong balance sheet and are well positioned to invest in our growth initiatives.

Now, I'd like to hand it over to Lisa, our Chief Merchandising Officer, to discuss our new product lines, and after that to David to discuss store operations.

Lisa Patel, Chief Merchandising Officer:
Thank you, Michael. This quarter, we launched our HearthStone kitchen and bath line, which has seen exceptional demand with comps up over 8% in the category. Private-label share gains undercut competitors while maintaining quality, and we're excited about the potential of this new product and other upcoming launches like sustainable textiles.

David Kwon, Chief Stores Officer:
Thank you, Lisa. We continue to focus on improving the customer experience in our stores. We have implemented 180 remodel prototypes with small-format footprints and immersive lifestyle zones, boosting sales per square foot 8% and seeing positive results across productivity metrics.

Now, let's open the line for questions.

Operator:
Thank you. As a reminder, please limit to one question and one follow-up. Our first question comes from Alex Rivera with Goldman Sachs. Please go ahead.

Alex Rivera (Goldman Sachs):
Good morning. Can you provide more color on the impact of the softening housing market on your sales?

Johnathan Reyes:
Thanks, Alex. Absolutely, the housing slowdown has pressured big-ticket durables like appliances and furniture, with NAR data showing 15% fewer existing home sales. However, we've offset this with strength in essentials—paint, tools, outdoor living—where traffic and ticket held firm. Sunbelt new starts in Florida and Texas drove +5.8% regional comps, and our project-oriented expertise keeps us resilient versus pure e-tail plays.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Emily Chen with JPMorgan. Please go ahead.

Emily Chen (JPMorgan):
What are your expectations for same-store sales growth in the next quarter?

Michael Chen:
Hi Emily. For Q4, we're guiding comps to +2.5% to +4.5%, reflecting holiday strength like Black Friday traffic up 8-10% from StoreFest events, Sunbelt housing tailwinds at 15% above national, and omnichannel BOPIS growth. We've pre-positioned 25% inventory and see acceleration from seasonal categories.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Robert Hayes with Barclays. Please go ahead.

Robert Hayes (Barclays):
Can you elaborate on the supply chain improvements?

Johnathan Reyes:
Sure, Robert. We've cut lead times 22% through Memphis DC expansion, vendor collaboration portals, and nearshoring to Mexico for hardlines, avoiding Red Sea ocean freight issues hitting softgoods peers. Multi-sourcing Asia/Mexico/domestic, forward contracts 70%, Maersk partnerships for 15% freight savings, and AI forecasting have optimized turns to 5.2x, supporting 95% in-stock and margin gains.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Laura Bennett with Morgan Stanley. Please go ahead.

Laura Bennett (Morgan Stanley):
What is the impact from the loyalty program?

Johnathan Reyes:
Great question, Laura. HomePro with 14 million members drove 22% attach on services, up significantly, contributing $180 million or 9% growth. Active usage +22% fueled 12% loyalty check-ins, 3.2 pps to comps via personalized nudges like mattress/sheets bundles lifting AUR 11%, and repeat visits 14% higher in key regions—core to our traffic and basket resilience.

Operator:
Our next question comes from Tom Vargas with Deutsche Bank. Please go ahead.

Tom Vargas (Deutsche Bank):
Just following up on gross margins—any more color on sustainability?

Michael Chen:
Thanks, Tom. The 120 bps expansion to 38.3% came from private-label mix now 28%, supply efficiencies like localized sourcing dropping freight to 4.2%, and RFID/AI curbing shrink to 1.1% and markdowns 25%. We're targeting another 100 bps H2 with 30% private-label ramp and micro-fulfillment, holding strong versus peers amid promo intensity.

Operator:
Thank you. That concludes today's Q&A. I'll now turn the call back over to Johnathan for closing remarks.

Johnathan Reyes, Chief Executive Officer:
Thank you for your questions. In closing, we are pleased with our progress this quarter and remain focused on executing our long-term strategy. Thank you for your continued support.

Sarah Thompson, Head of Investor Relations:
This concludes today's call. Thank you for joining us.
